reviewMethod: Source review of the S1API 3.2.3 NPC/customer/supplier and native schedule surfaces, plus S1API 3.2.2 shop AddItem pricing surface, S1MAPI 2.0.1 procedural building APIs, plus the Daffy's Hills 1.2 reference archive. Focused runtime API scanner and procedural warehouse factory are included. GitHub Actions verifies compile/package/static tests only; Schedule I in-game generation, door behavior, navigation, Realtor transaction and saves remain unverified. The NPC schedule layer now uses S1API 3.2.3 prefab-time SitAtSeatSet for a single pilot routine and exports read-only native NavMesh/seat-set reachability data; no in-game movement is claimed until a user runtime survey confirms it.

statusLegend.implemented_code_unverified_runtime: Code exists and builds, but target-game execution is not confirmed.
statusLegend.design_only: Requirements/data exist as a plan or configuration, not executable runtime behavior.
statusLegend.not_implemented: No connected implementation exists in this repository.
statusLegend.blocked_unverified_api: The public registration/integration path has not been established from the inspected API.
statusLegend.not_verified_in_game: Requires the installed game, save data, or runtime output.

requirements.requirement: Create functional native buildings and enterable interiors.
evidence: src/Runtime/HarborlineProceduralBuildingFactory.cs uses reflection to invoke S1MAPI BuildingBuilder/BuildingConfig for procedural floor, walls, roof and lights.
A server-side S1MAPI AddSlidingDoors call is attempted for the warehouse entrance; if the installed API surface differs, the original primitive shell fallback remains.
NavigationBuilder.CreateNavigationBuilder().Build() is attempted for interior A* navigation; this is not the city street graph and is not an enterable native Property registration.
requirements.remaining: Verify BuildingBuilder method signatures and visible placement in the target game; test door open/manual interaction, network replication, interior NPC pathing and save/load. Replace temporary interior rack/counter props with functional native prefabs. The warehouse is not yet registered as a native Building/Property/Business.

requirements.requirement: Spawn 42 physical native NPCs, initially activate about 18, with 2 dealers.
evidence: src/Runtime/HarborlineNpcRoster.cs: 2 native PlayerDealer NPCs, 8 physical native Customer NPCs and 1 native supplier/dead-drop/meeting NPC.
HarborlineNpcRegistrar registers eleven stable IDs after CustomNpcsReady; NPC.Get(id) prevents duplicates.
HarborlinePhysicalBuilder supplies eleven local spawn slots, but their walkability and routing have not been tested.
requirements.remaining: Eleven of 42 target physical NPCs are coded (2 dealers, 8 customers, 1 supplier); 31 remain. Only 8 of 30 customer profiles are complete; 22 remain. Confirm all eleven spawn, have correct dialogue, use the correct native role, and persist across save/load.

requirements.requirement: Use native NPC schedules and allow NPCs to enter buildings.
evidence: All eight customer types use IsCustomer=true; S1API 3.2.3 configures native customer deal-attendance behaviour without the obsolete NPCSignal_WaitForDelivery.
HarborlineNpcLifecycle enables each native NPC schedule through NPC.Schedule.Enable().

Maya Bennett has a prefab-time S1API WithSchedule plan using SitAtSeatSet against the existing Docks WaterFront/OutdoorBench (1) AvatarSeatSet at 14:30 for 30 in-game minutes. The game owns seat resolution, pathfinding, movement and sitting.
NativeNavigationSurveyExporter records the live Unity NavMesh.SamplePosition/CalculatePath results and real AvatarSeatSet hierarchy paths from the installed game.
requirements.remaining: The Maya waterfront routine and pathfinding still require in-game verification. Add more customer routines only after native-seat-sets.csv and harborline-spawn-navigation.csv confirm real reachable seat sets/routes. StayInBuilding actions wait until Harborline buildings are registered in the native Building registry; do not use the procedural shell as a substitute. Dealer work/home behaviour remains owned by native DealerAttendDealBehaviour and HomeEvent.

evidence: src/Diagnostics/NativeLawSnapshotExporter.cs uses S1API.Law reflection to export LawController/LawManager values and CheckpointManager.GetAllCheckpointInfo.
Exports native-law-checkpoint-locations.csv, native-law-checkpoints.csv, native-law-foot-patrol-routes.csv and native-law-vehicle-patrol-routes.csv.
The snapshot is read-only and does not enable a checkpoint or start a patrol.
requirements.remaining: Run the exporter in the target Schedule I installation and inspect all six native-law-*.csv files; confirm actual loaded wrapper members and route coordinates before changing law coverage.

overallVerdict: The repository now contains a native S1API gameplay slice (2 dealers, 8 customers and 1 supplier using the dead-drop/meeting flow), a 14-item Hardware Store extension, and a procedural Harborline warehouse path using S1MAPI BuildingBuilder with a guarded primitive fallback. The S1MAPI door and interior A* calls are code-level integrations only and still require in-game validation. A focused read-only API scanner was added for Realtor, ownership, doors, navigation, roads and map hooks. Native schedule definitions now include one S1API SitAtSeatSet pilot for Maya; actual movement remains runtime-unverified. The reference Daffy's Hills archive was inspected for architecture only; no code/assets were copied. 11 of the target 42 NPCs are coded, with 31 remaining; 8 of 30 customer profiles are coded, with 22 remaining. Separate Harborline storefront/phone orders, Realtor listing/ownership registration, normal map integration, city roads, full routines, police extension, persistence and multiplayer remain incomplete or blocked.

validation.caveat: CI compile/package/static tests do not prove Unity/IL2CPP runtime behavior, BuildingBuilder calls, server-spawned door creation, NPC pathfinding, transactions or persistence.
